disease_label_per_paper: Occult perforated gangrenous gallbladder found on MRCP
presentation_summary: 69-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes, and recent right pontine infarct arrived from rehabilitation as a stroke alert after fall and altered mental status.
He reported right-sided/right upper quadrant abdominal pain rated 3/10 that had started about four weeks earlier.
He was hemodynamically stable and did not meet SIRS criteria; exam showed mild right upper quadrant tenderness.
Labs included WBC 11.8 thousand/mL, alkaline phosphatase 259 U/L, AST 259 U/L, lipase 721 U/L, and CRP 18 mg/dL.
Ultrasound showed acute cholecystitis with pericholecystic fluid; CT showed acute cholecystitis with fluid communication with the liver but no abscess.
MRCP within the early hospitalization showed perforated gangrenous cholecystitis with subcapsular abscess/phlegmonous change.
